gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Bambu Lab P2S's own '50 °C chamber' figure is a passive limit with no heater: it comes from bed heat held in by an automatic air flap, and owners log about 37–52 °C depending on the aux-fan setting. The QIDI Q2's '65 °C' is a setpoint held by a dedicated 280 W chamber heater. The two figures look comparable but are not.
standout_why: I read three rival pages. firstlayerlab.com (cited) lists P1S/P2S/K1C chamber temperature as 'Not stated' and calls the P2S 'Passive, with an airflow flap'. It gives the Q2 '65 °C active PTC' but no heater wattage. 3dprintgearlab.com (cited) says the P2S has 'no active heating listed', gives no chamber number and no heater power, and only adds the general line 'Enclosed isn't heated'. layerwalker.com (rank 3) gives a general 35–45 °C for passive boxes but no P2S number, and does not mention Bambu's 50 °C claim or the aux-fan effect. None of them puts Bambu's 50 °C figure next to QIDI's 65 °C on the same basis (heater watts and how the temperature is reached), and none cites owner logs that show the P2S range moving with the fan setting. I could not open Popular Mechanics (cited) or The Verge (fetch blocked), so I can't say what they contain.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's split pick. For PLA and PETG, the P2S's passive chamber is enough. For ABS, ASA and nylon, the Q2 at the same $449 has a 280 W heater that holds 65 °C. The P2S's 50 °C is a best case that one owner logged at 37–42 °C with the right aux fan at 100% in heating mode. It also warns shoppers off the QIDI Q2C ($349): it has the same 270 × 270 × 256 mm build volume, but its US store blurb doesn't list chamber heating, while the Q2's blurb does.
